title: Integer Break
statement: Break the integer `n` into at least two positive integers that sum to n. Return the maximum product of those integers. Order does not matter.
hints: dp[x] is the maximum product of a break of x. It may also be useful to keep x unbroken when it is a part of a larger number.
For a part, the best contribution is max(k, dp[k]), except the original n must be broken at least once.
The math shortcut is to break into as many 3s as possible, and avoid a remainder of 1 by using a 4 = 2 + 2 instead of 3 + 1.

approaches.name: Break into threes
approaches.explanation: The optimal part size is 3, with the remainder-1 exception.

editorial: For the DP, dp[i] = max over k < i of k * max(i - k, dp[i - k]). The max with the unbroken remainder is what lets a part stay whole. The closed form prefers 3s because 3 gives a better product per unit than 2 or 4, while 1 is never a useful part. 4 is the exception: 2 * 2 beats 3 * 1.
